chapters.title: Ancient Guardians
chapters.description: Immortal keepers, dying dragons, and living boundaries carry memory before recorded states.
chapters.sequenceNote: A deep-history affinity, not proof that these guardians share a land or generation.

chapters.title: First Gifts & Compacts
chapters.description: Village gifts, names, night creatures, heroic callings, and patient wards turn wild power into custom.
chapters.sequenceNote: These are early magical forms; their internal order and common ancestry remain open.

chapters.title: Old Towers & First Guests
chapters.description: Ancient dwellings and rural refuges make hospitality the first durable magical institution.
chapters.sequenceNote: The shared shape is old, inhabited magic; no common road or chronology is asserted.

chapters.title: Roads, Markets & Living Doors
chapters.description: Trade, repair, shelter circuits, and bearer-powered crossings let wonder travel between communities.
chapters.sequenceNote: A civic-road phase fit; the doors and markets are not one system.

chapters.title: Founding Legends
chapters.description: Commoners, impossible champions, and returned royal signs become the stories kingdoms build upon.
chapters.sequenceNote: Grouped by founding scale rather than one dynasty or continent.

chapters.title: Succession & Broken Prophecy
chapters.description: Vacant thrones, divided heirs, altered sisters, and refused futures make succession unstable.
chapters.sequenceNote: These succession crises share a political maturity, not a family tree.

chapters.title: Dragon Polities
chapters.description: Dragon alliances and disguised rulers turn catastrophe management into government and peace.
chapters.sequenceNote: The local Crown of Quiet Hours sequence is preserved; no wider dragon empire is implied.

chapters.title: Saints, Demons & Monster Sanctuaries
chapters.description: Religious office, forbidden love, monster refuge, and merciful power contest who deserves protection.
chapters.sequenceNote: Sacred and monstrous labels are local; the stories establish no universal theology.

chapters.title: Healers, Blood & Bounded Bodies
chapters.description: Orders of healing begin measuring blood, training, injury, justice, and the limits of repair.
chapters.sequenceNote: A mature healing culture fit; the practices remain locally bounded.

chapters.title: Guilds, Gods & Repair
chapters.description: Legendary makers and accidental civic divinity turn magical competence into public responsibility.
chapters.sequenceNote: The shared fit is professionalized power, not one guild or pantheon.

chapters.title: Schools, Houses & Classification
chapters.description: Magic is sorted into houses, bodily signs, assessments, and institutions that can be challenged.
chapters.sequenceNote: A shared institutional phase; the schools and classifications are independent.

chapters.title: Arcane Infrastructure & Engineered Peril
chapters.description: Persistent sunsets, hostile systems, mills, and higher-order machines make wonder an engineering problem.
chapters.sequenceNote: A late old-magic industry fit; these mechanisms do not share an inventor.

chapters.eyebrow: Relative link · one master, later apprentice
chapters.title: Colleges & Apprenticeship Reform
chapters.description: Kethra's qualification and later apprenticeship preserve a local sequence inside institutional magecraft.
chapters.sequenceNote: Only the relationship between these two stories is linked; the wider era remains a fit.

chapters.title: Constructed Life at Cinder Annex
chapters.description: A school treats living magic, engineered friends, and accessible systems as teachable craft.
chapters.sequenceNote: Its civilizational shape fits arcane industry; the Annex's physical-world relation and side of zero remain unresolved.

chapters.title: The Old Modern Age
chapters.description: A modern human civilization spans a changing magical-girl age, from ordinary public abundance to hidden local teams, rare ultrahuman power, and the long fade before the Glass-Sea era.
chapters.sequenceNote: Not About That precedes the Battle of the Bay while magical girls remain numerous. Separately, Northbridge incident → Help Network → Battle of the Bay → The Dress They Brought Her; the post-battle misidentification precedes the later museum visit.

chapters.title: The Ravel Bridge
chapters.description: Nell and Bash touch the old low-magic modernity while Ravel remains another undated era of the same physical world.
chapters.sequenceNote: The unequal clocks and old-modern endpoint are fixed; Ravel's universal coordinate is not.

chapters.title: The Glass-Sea Age
chapters.description: The Day of Glass begins a four-century regional aftermath that ends with a second dawn.
chapters.sequenceNote: Fixed after the Battle of the Bay; its relationship to most undated civilizations stays open.

chapters.eyebrow: Relative link · side of zero unknown
chapters.title: The Museum Hinge
chapters.description: Centuries after the Battle of the Bay, its last witness corrects the museum record.
chapters.sequenceNote: The story is later than Solstice Evening Bell but not bounded relative to All Accounts Due.

chapters.title: All Accounts Due
chapters.description: Every old magic-active material history reaches one hard stop. Six systems fall permanently to zero.
chapters.sequenceNote: Fixed extinction boundary: no powered remnant crosses into the Long Dark.

chapters.title: Colossi & Buried Engines
chapters.description: Civilizations live around impossible-seeming stone bodies and endless mechanisms sustained by material causes.
chapters.sequenceNote: A Long Dark candidate fit; monumental appearance is not evidence of operative magic.

chapters.title: Altered Memory & Valley Medicine
chapters.description: Water, plants, memory, poison, and medicine create wonder through rare natural systems.
chapters.sequenceNote: A material-ecology hypothesis; neither story proves a universal date.

chapters.title: Bodies Outside the Old Measure
chapters.description: Caravans, serpentfolk, and dungeon survivors inhabit a material world broader than one human norm.
chapters.sequenceNote: Creature form does not imply magic; these cultures share no proven kingdom.

chapters.title: Refuge Courts & Marriage States
chapters.description: Hidden princesses, imperial walls, strategic marriages, and military treaties sustain nonmagical states.
chapters.sequenceNote: A shared courtly morphology, not one royal lineage.

chapters.title: Creature Cultures Without Enchantment
chapters.description: Dragons, adventurers, slimes, and catfolk belong to societies whose local causes need no spell system.
chapters.sequenceNote: A deliberately material fantasy-age fit; biology and custom are not treated as magic.

chapters.title: Guild Blades, Gaslight Houses & Engineers
chapters.description: Dueling custom, named tools, unreliable engineering, and status houses produce a fantasy-shaped material modernity.
chapters.sequenceNote: A civic-technology phase fit; no shared city or industrial revolution is asserted.

chapters.title: Ordinary Present & Familiar Lives
chapters.description: Friendship, festivals, bodies, cafés, and ordinary social pressure define a recognizably material present.
chapters.sequenceNote: These modern-shaped lives are compatible with our era without being one city or exact year.

chapters.title: Private Powers & Public States
chapters.description: Crime networks, governments, and unusual individuals exercise material power without a public magic order.
chapters.sequenceNote: Political scale separates these stories from both ordinary life and superhero modernity.

chapters.title: Anomalies Beside Material Zero
chapters.description: A modern death and an impossible sky touch familiar material lives while their larger ontologies resist dating.
chapters.sequenceNote: The living frames suggest the Long Dark; the station and cosmic anomaly themselves remain coordinate-open.

chapters.title: Layered & Networked Cities
chapters.description: Architectural layers, class interfaces, surveillance, and autonomous traffic make the city itself a governing system.
chapters.sequenceNote: A networked-modernity grouping; the cities are independent designs.

chapters.title: Synthetic Bodies & War Legacies
chapters.description: Mutable bodies, bionics, android veterans, and respawn spectacle push personhood through engineered systems.
chapters.sequenceNote: A synthetic-modernity phase, not one technology stack or political order.

chapters.title: Great Falls & Salvage
chapters.description: Floating cities fail, launch rooms wait, names outlive wreckage, and exposed seas reveal prior orders.
chapters.sequenceNote: Each fall keeps its own cause and successor history; the markers do not share one collapse.

chapters.title: Mobile Cities & Restored Bodies
chapters.description: Rebel bodies, solarpunk weather, living housing, migratory cities, and delayed warnings define successor worlds.
chapters.sequenceNote: A post-fall technology morphology; no common recovery or planet is asserted.

chapters.title: Orbital Watchers & Successor Earths
chapters.description: Jovian defenders, ancient sunshades, handmade kites, and a dinosaur Earth preserve independent orbital histories.
chapters.sequenceNote: The Apes Above keeps its own exodus sequence; the other markers share no required launch.

chapters.title: Archive Refoundings
chapters.description: Excavations, leased memory, and an injured starship make forgotten civilizations legible to later lives.
chapters.sequenceNote: Each story preserves its own deep interval; no common archive age is claimed.

chapters.title: The Sky Remembers Us
chapters.description: After ages of perfect absence, living people on both sides of the sky originate reciprocal magic.
chapters.sequenceNote: Fixed reawakening boundary: genuinely new magic begins here; the six old systems remain dead.

chapters.title: Time, Foresight & Copies
chapters.description: Clairvoyance, repeated Tuesdays, and a duplicated self make the return of magic intimate before it is public.
chapters.sequenceNote: A hidden-return phase fit; joined-sky ancestry remains unproven.

chapters.title: Inheritances & Altered Selves
chapters.description: Curses, possession, artifacts, advising animals, and transformed partners carry magic through private relationships.
chapters.sequenceNote: A domestic post-return grouping; the mechanisms remain independent.

chapters.title: Visitors at the Door
chapters.description: Necromantic families, animal visitors, angels, and an infernal royal gate turn private thresholds into relationships.
chapters.sequenceNote: Grouped by domestic crossings, not one species, afterlife, or portal network.

chapters.title: The Assignment Bridge
chapters.description: One modern apartment brackets ten bodily crossings whose worlds keep their own histories.
chapters.sequenceNote: Ryo's departure and return supply the working coordinate; the ten destinations do not inherit it.

chapters.title: Monsters, Gods & Avatars
chapters.description: Monster industries, regenerating gods, earthly champions, and domestic villainy become publicly legible.
chapters.sequenceNote: A public-power phase; these figures share no pantheon or institution.

chapters.title: Transformations Become Public
chapters.description: True forms, shapeshifting, shrinking powers, and thermal bodies become ordinary social knowledge.
chapters.sequenceNote: This is a magical modernity, deliberately separate from the ordinary Long Dark present.

chapters.title: Hero & Villain Institutions
chapters.description: Hero families, villain households, magical illness, and combat schooling form a distinct public-power society.
chapters.sequenceNote: A dedicated superhero-era fit; it is not our ordinary modernity with exceptions added.

chapters.title: Threshold Transit & Unstable Travel
chapters.description: Lightning, sleep, buses, and licensed living seams make impossible travel part of modern life.
chapters.sequenceNote: A crossing-modernity fit; destinations and mechanisms remain separate.

chapters.title: Civic Myth & Dangerous Archives
chapters.description: Town debts, artifact collections, memory therapy, and fatal media give modern institutions mythic depth.
chapters.sequenceNote: A later integrated-magic phase; contemporary appearance alone fixes no date.

chapters.title: Second-Sky Kingdoms
chapters.description: A later magical sky kingdom proves that fantasy-shaped polities can rise again after modernity.
chapters.sequenceNote: A provisional post-Sky home: the story's active wards exclude the Long Dark, but do not prove this exact distance from reawakening.
